nodes.title: Blueprint decision 9, per-line half: a catastrophic line is caught by about calls 13-15 and its script slowed to 25%. Learning's harm lane (18c4fd4: 2 harm moments in 15 calls) catches harm classes; this catches one line of hers that people keep reacting badly to. DESIGN. (1) script.line_check {conversationId} (calls, draft) runs after every analysed live call, next to script.harm_check; window = the script's (agent version's) last 15 analysed live calls that ended after its last restore; test calls never count. (2) A line is one agent turn, normalised: lower case, letters and digits in any script, digits as #, the contact's own name tokens and 1-character tokens dropped; two lines are the same line when their token sets overlap with Jaccard >= 0.7 (greedy, in call order; the first seen is the one quoted). (3) A bad reaction is attributed to one line: a caller hang-up (END_EARLY_HANGUP, END_HUNG_UP_MID) to her last line; an opt-out (a caller line the safety floor reads as opt-out, or an opt_out moment) to her line just before it; anger (reason CONV_COMPLAINT) to her line just before the first objection moment's caller line, else her last line. Each line counts once per call for 'said' and once for 'bad'. (4) Trip: a line said in n calls of the window with bad reactions in k of them trips when k >= 3 and the one-sided binomial P(X >= k | n, p0) < 0.01. p0 = 0.35 for her opening line (the early-hang-up monitor's own threshold, so an opener with an ordinary hang-up rate never trips: it needs 5 of 5, 6 of 7, 7 of 8 or 11 of 15) and p0 = 0.15 for any later line (ASSUMED, not measured: a bad reaction right after one mid-call line is rarer than an early hang-up; it trips at 3 of 3, 4 of 5, 5 of 8). (5) On a trip: learning's script_throttle row (factor 0.25, detail.signal 'catastrophic_line', her line quoted, the calls, k of n) so campaigns' G12 slows the script with no new hook; a critical Safety issue on the agent version; and an alert: a trigger on script_throttle puts 'script.slowed' on the outbox and notifications send it as 'A script was slowed' (this also alerts on learning's harm throttles). script.pacing.restore (learning) restores either. No model call; only her words are quoted, never the caller's.
nodes.rationale: Integrator task (must-be audit, decision 9). Separate signal from learning's harm moments; one throttle table, one restore.
nodes.reverse_if: On real traffic, a benign script trips more than once per 1,000 script-days, or a planted catastrophic line in a synthetic set does not trip by call 15, or the 50-call early-hang-up monitor flags the same lines first in most cases (then this adds nothing). Or measured per-line bad-reaction rates on real mid-call lines sit near or above 0.15 (then p0 is wrong and benign lines trip).
evidence: product/tests/calls-line-watch.test.ts (synthetic, fictional): a line said every other call with 4 in 5 bad reactions trips by call 15 (pure stream and on the real modules, one analysed call at a time); a benign 45-call stream (opener with 4 in 15 early hang-ups, one opt-out, one complaint after different lines) never trips; the analysis bench's 84 hand-written calls in windows of 15 never trip; the throttle row (0.25, signal catastrophic_line), the critical Safety issue quoting her line with no name or caller words, and one 'script.slowed' notification delivery in words with no ids

nodes.title: Catastrophic-line lane on synthetic calls (n: 1 planted stream of 30 calls, 1 benign stream of 45, the bench's 84 cases; method: catastrophicLine over every prefix in windows of 15, and script.line_check on the real modules with calls written one by one). Planted line trips by call 15 (asserted <= 15); benign stream and bench: 0 trips. Not measured: real traffic, real per-line reaction rates (p0 0.15 for mid-call lines is assumed), and how often it trips before the 50-call early-hang-up monitor would.

events.details: Design written before the build, per the integrator.

Full suite on a fresh DB 785/786: the one red is the suite's browser run, which could not drop vp_web_e2e because web/e2e/run.sh leaves its dev server (product/web/dev/serve.ts) running after a standalone run; the browser flows pass 76/76 standalone. run.sh's cleanup is web's; noted, not fixed here.
